_signal_classes_why: Rule RET-001, 16 September 2026. The return-path rule asks what a net's spectral content deserves, so every signal net needs a class and a reason. A net matched by no entry here is UNKNOWN and is judged at the STRICTEST bar, so an omission costs a failure rather than buying a pass. Patterns are shell globs over the net name without its leading slash, first match wins.

signal_classes.basis: USB 1.1 full speed at 12 Mbit/s into the RP2040's own transceiver: the bit rate is slow and the EDGES are nanoseconds, which is what the return path sees
signal_classes.rise_basis: USB 2.0 full speed: the specification's own minimum transition time, TFR/TFF 4 ns 10 to 90 percent (Table 7-9). The bit rate is 40 times slower than high speed and the edge only 8 times

signal_classes.basis: the RP2040's QSPI flash bus, clocked to 133 MHz by the chip's own ROM bootloader (RP2040 datasheet, XIP interface)
the 12 MHz crystal oscillator's drive node, a continuous periodic source and its loop is the classic emitter
the other half of the same 12 MHz oscillator loop
a converter switch node: the fastest edges on this board and its primary radiated source, so it is held to the strict criterion whatever its data rate
the LT8705A tracker's two switch nodes, as above
the tracker's bootstrap nodes, which ride on the switch nodes and carry the same edges
the tracker's top gate drives: amperes into a FET gate in nanoseconds
the tracker's bottom gate drives, as above
a bootstrap node riding on a switch node
the hot-swap FET gate: slew-limited by design, but it is a gate drive and is held to the strict bar
the fan FET's gate drive, switched by the 25 kHz PWM: a gate node with nanosecond edges
a FET gate drive
I2C at 100 or 400 kHz with an open-drain pull-up: the edge is set by the pull-up and the bus capacitance, tens to hundreds of nanoseconds
the data half of the same I2C bus
the SWD debug port, a few MHz and used only on a bench with a probe attached
the IMU's SPI chip select and its interrupt line, both driven by the RP2040 at a few MHz at most
the fan PWM at 25 kHz, a logic-level square wave with fast edges into a gate

the fan tachometer, two pulses a revolution through a pull-up: under a kilohertz, and the edge is the pull-up's RC rather than a driver's. Declared CLOCKED_DIGITAL until 16 September 2026, which contradicted this very sentence: the class is what the spectral content is, and a sub-kilohertz open-drain line pulled up by a resistor has none worth a return path. It is corrected here because the basis was already right, not because a rule was refusing the board
a counted pulse input (Geiger, DCF77): the rate is low and the edge is a comparator's, so it is treated as clocked rather than DC
the lightning sensor's interrupt: an edge into a GPIO, rare but not slow
a resistor-divider voltage monitor into an ADC input: a DC level with a filter capacitor on it
a sense line (water level, current sense): a DC or near-DC level read by an ADC or an amplifier
the water probe's excitation, a DC level through a series resistor
the cold-charge and shore inhibit, a static level through an optocoupler that changes state at most a few times a day
a reset or run input, a static level with an RC on it
a shutdown enable, a static level
a power-good flag, an open-drain static level
the RP2040 boot-select jumper, a static level read once at reset
an indicator LED's anode or cathode, a static level or a slow blink
the hot-swap controller's timer, sense and undervoltage and overvoltage set pins: RC levels and divider taps, deliberately slow
the tracker's feedback divider taps: a DC level inside the control loop, filtered
the tracker's current-sense inputs across a shunt: millivolts of DC with a filter
the tracker's current-monitor outputs, a DC level
the tracker's line-sense input, a divider tap
the tracker's error-amplifier compensation node, a capacitor and a resistor to ground
the tracker's soft-start capacitor node, a ramp of milliseconds
the tracker's frequency-setting resistor node, a DC bias
the tracker's internal LDO output, a local supply with its own decoupling
the tracker's 3.3 V LDO output, a local supply
the tracker's gate-drive supply rail, decoupled at the pin
a regulator's internal-supply decoupling node, a local supply
a chip's digital supply pin with its decoupling, a local rail
the Geiger tube's anode feed through its series resistor: a high-impedance DC bias, not a signal edge
a spare contact on the dock block, unconnected to any driver
the isolated converter's secondary-side return reference, a DC node

_annular_min_mm_why: Rule VIA-002. JLCPCB rigid PCB manufacturing capabilities, annular ring rows, read 16 September 2026 (v2/vendor/fabricator/jlcpcb-pcb-capabilities-2026-09-16.md): four layers at 1 oz outer: multilayer 1 oz, recommended 0.20 mm or above. The RECOMMENDED figure is taken and not the absolute minimum, because the absolute minimum is where yield starts to suffer and this board is made five at a time with no second chance before the owner has it in his hands.
_via_ring_min_mm_why: Rule VIA-002, the VIA rows rather than the annular ring row. JLCPCB rigid PCB manufacturing capabilities, read 16 September 2026 (v2/vendor/fabricator/jlcpcb-pcb-capabilities-2026-09-16.md): minimum via diameter 0.25 mm on a minimum via hole of 0.15 mm for 2 or more layers, which leaves 0.05 mm of copper per side. The PTH annular ring row (0.20 mm) is stated for a plated COMPONENT hole and cannot bind a via, because no via at this document's own minimum could satisfy it; board D12 was refused on 16 September for a 0.45/0.20 via at 0.125 mm of ring, which is what that confusion costs.
_copper_layers_why: Four layers as built; E gets an In2 ground fill under decision 27 rather than another layer.

external_ports.why: shore and vehicle DC entry from the MIL-DTL-38999 wall receptacle
the solar input, a long outdoor lead by definition
the outside climate and ultraviolet sensor pod, through an M8 sealed receptacle on the connector plate

_external_ports_why: Rule TRN-001, 16 September 2026. A port that leaves the ENCLOSURE is a wire a person will plug something into, in the rain, having walked across a floor. Every one of them reaches a semiconductor, and the only thing between is a suppressor, a choke, a series resistor into a clamp, or nothing. Most connectors on these boards are internal (board-to-board ribbons, module sockets, fan leads inside a sealed case) and treating every J as external would refuse every board for wires that never leave it. The board knows which is which and nothing else does, so each one is named with where it goes.

GND.what: the board's ground, the reference for everything after the input filter, and the return the dock block carries to board A

GND_V.what: the VEHICLE-SIDE return, from the DC inlet through the fuse, the ideal diode and the hot-swap to the input filter. It is NOT an isolation barrier and must not be read as one: it meets GND through the second winding of the SRF1260 common-mode choke, so the two are joined at DC and separated only for common-mode current. The isolated barrier on this kit is the TRACO TEN 40 further down, and it has its own secondary
GND_V._signals_why: both are referenced across the partition on purpose and both are slow: DCIN_PGD is the LM5069's power-good going to the controller, and SHORE_INHIBIT is the opto inhibit that stops charging in the cold. Each crosses at the choke, which is the one place the two returns meet, so neither makes a loop that the partition exists to prevent

_grounds_why: 16 September 2026, rule GND-001: either the board has one ground and says so, or every partition is drawn deliberately with its crossing points named and the signals that cross listed. ground_system.py reads the netlist and compares it with this.
critical_k_why: l = t_r / (6 t_pd). ECSS-E-HB-20-07A section 6.1.2.3 works a real case where a 35 mm clock track with a 200 ps edge failed a radiated emission test: that track is ONE rise distance long (t_r / t_pd = 34.5 mm on its microstrip), which is k = 1, and the handbook calls it a textbook radiator. k = 2 is half a known failure and k = 6 is a sixth of it. The number is this project's choice; the handbook is what it was calibrated against, and no standard in this tree states a value for k

Y1.source: Abracon ABM8-272-T3, load capacitance 10 pF, read from the RP2040 hardware design guide section 2.3.1, which names this exact part and works this exact arithmetic: two 15 pF capacitors give 7.5 pF in series, the pins and tracks add about 3 pF, and 10.5 pF is close enough to the target of 10
Y1._stray_why: 3 pF, the allowance the RP2040 hardware design guide uses for the pins and tracks of a 3225 crystal beside its IC, which is the geometry every crystal on these boards has

_sense_clearance_why: BOARD E'S TWO ANA-001 FAILURES, and which of them a class could fix (17 September 2026). TRK_LSENSE runs 0.209 mm from TRK_SW2 over 2.71 mm against a declared 0.50, and WATER_SENSE 0.556 mm from TRK_SW1 over 20.49 mm against a declared 1.00. Both nets sit in class PWR, whose clearance is 0.15 mm, so the router did what it was told. Measured pad edge to pad edge before proposing a class: TRK_LSENSE's three pads are 1.760, 0.850 and 2.890 mm from the nearest other-net pad, so a 0.50 mm class WOULD escape every one of them; WATER_SENSE's are 2.000, 0.850, 0.650 and **0.200 mm at U10 pin 38**, the controller's own fine-pitch pin, so its declared 1.00 mm cannot be a class at all. What is NOT settled here is whether TRK_LSENSE should leave PWR: it lands on L1 pad 2, the tracker inductor's own terminal, so it may be carrying current rather than sensing it, and a class that narrows it to a signal width would be wrong. That is a circuit question for board E's next generation, which is also when decision 31's clamps land, and the measurement above is what it needs.

_e_floorplan_why: WHY BOARD E KEEPS LEAVING A HANDFUL OF LONG NETS OPEN, measured 18 September 2026 16:00 UTC on E18's placed board. The strip is 267 x 68 mm and **U10, the QFN-56 sensor controller, sits at x 236, the far east end, while 26 of its signal nets have a partner more than 40 mm WEST and NOT ONE has a far partner east**: SDA0, SDA1, SCL1 and the +3V3_E6 pins reach x 5 to 6, which is 230 mm away, and the five nets E18 left open (DCF_PULSE, DCIN_PGD, FAN2_PWM, FAN2_TACH over 182 to 227 mm, plus the local GEIGER_PULSE at 37 mm) are that same crossing. So every sensor signal on this board traverses the whole strip. **What this is NOT: the cause of the opens, and E17 is the counter-example** (the same U10 seat, three parts different, 0 hard and 0 unrouted after its closers). The router is deterministic and this floor plan sits at the edge of what it can close, so a three-part change resamples it and lands anywhere between 0 and 5 open. That makes the opens SCATTER on a hard floor plan rather than a property of the design, which is why more rounds keep buying connections (round 2's via-cost remedy took five to four). **The durable answer is a redistribution**, U10 and its decoupling west into the sensor cluster or the headers east, which on this strip is a floor-plan campaign like board B's and not a router setting; the occupancy is fairly even (28 parts in x 0-20, 25 in 180-200, 25 in 240-260), so there is no empty band to move into and the move costs somebody else's seat. The cheap answer is what routeflow is doing: keep rounds on E18's placement until one lands at zero.
